content.1_the_two_tools_and_what_each_does:
| Tool | Role | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| `xcodebuild` | Compile, codesign, and (optionally) produce a `.xcarchive` / `.app` / `.ipa` from an `.xcodeproj` or `.xcworkspace` | Lives at `xcodebuild` (run via `/usr/bin/xcodebuild` or `xcrun xcodebuild`) |
| `xcrun devicectl` | Interact with physical Apple devices: install, launch, terminate, query, capture logs | Ships inside Xcode at `Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/PrivateFrameworks/CoreDevice.framework/.../bin/devicectl`; you always invoke it through `xcrun devicectl` so the active Xcode is selected |

iPad hardware runs iPadOS, but from `xcodebuild`'s perspective it is treated as the `iOS` platform. The destination specifier, the SDK, and the deployment target are all `iOS`.

content.2_xcodebuild_flags_that_matter_for_a_phy:
### 2.1 Core flags you must pass

```
xcodebuild \
    -workspace MyApp.xcworkspace \      # or -project MyApp.xcodeproj
    -scheme MyApp \
    -configuration Release \
    -destination 'platform=iOS,name=Joe's iPad' \   # or id=<UDID>, or generic
    -derivedDataPath build \
    CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 \
    CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Development" \
    -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    -allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration \
    build
```

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-workspace` / `-project` | Choose between CocoaPods/SPM workspace and a raw project. Use `-workspace` whenever you have one. |
| `-scheme` | The active scheme (must be **Shared**, otherwise CI agents can't see it). |
| `-configuration` | `Debug` or `Release`. For TestFlight/App Store use `Release`; for ad-hoc use `Debug`. |
| `-destination` | Tells `xcodebuild` the target. Three useful forms (see 2.2). |
| `-derivedDataPath` | Optional. Pin output to a known location (`build/Build/Products/...`). |
| `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` | Build setting that turns on automatic signing for the whole project from the CLI. |
| `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<TeamID>` | Your 10-char Apple Developer team ID. Required for automatic signing. |
| `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Development"` | "Apple Development" for debug, "Apple Distribution" for release/TestFlight. For a generic device build that will be later exported, omit and let automatic signing pick. |
| `-allowProvisioningUpdates` | Lets `xcodebuild` talk to Apple and create/refresh provisioning profiles on the fly. Equivalent to clicking "Fix Issue" in Xcode. |
| `-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration` | Lets `xcodebuild` register the connected iPad with the dev portal the first time you deploy. |

### 2.2 Destination specifiers (the `=` values matter)

| Specifier | Meaning | When to use |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `generic/platform=iOS` | Build a `.app` for "any iOS device" without needing one attached | Archive + export workflows |
| `platform=iOS,id=<UDID>` | Build for the specific iPad whose UDID matches | One-off CI jobs targeting one device |
| `platform=iOS,name='Joe's iPad'` | Build for a device by its user-given name | Local development, the device name is shown in Finder |
| `platform=iOS,OS=18.0` | Pin to an iOS version (combines with `id` or `name`) | Reproducibility in CI |

> Tip: `xcrun xctrace list devices` and `xcrun devicectl list devices` both report device UDIDs and names. `devicectl` is the modern equivalent.

### 2.3 Build-only vs. archive vs. test

```
xcodebuild ... build                                 # default; produces .app
xcodebuild ... archive -archivePath build/MyApp.xcarchive
xcodebuild ... build-for-testing                      # produce .xctestrun + .app
xcodebuild ... test-without-building -resultBundlePath ...  # needs xctestrun
```

For a typical "build and deploy to a real iPad" pipeline you usually:

1. `xcodebuild ... build` → produces `build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/MyApp.app`
2. `devicectl device install app --device <UDID> MyApp.app`
3. `devicectl device process launch --device <UDID> com.example.myapp`

### 2.4 Cleaning and inspecting the output

```
xcodebuild -workspace MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp clean build
```

If you need a single-machine IPA for distribution: archive, then export with an `ExportOptions.plist` (see §4).

content.3_automatic_code_signing_flags_what_each:
These four flags/keys are the entire "automatic provisioning" surface in `xcodebuild`:

| Flag / Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `-allowProvisioningUpdates` | `xcodebuild` will fetch or update provisioning profiles from your developer account on demand. Required any time you do not already have a valid profile locally (e.g. new bundle ID, new device). |
| `-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration` | On first deploy, `xcodebuild` will register the connected iPad's UDID in your team. Convenient for dev fleets; many teams disable this in production CI and pre-register devices instead. |
| `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` | Project-level build setting that enables automatic signing for the whole target. Without this, manual profile files (`*.mobileprovision`) are expected. |
| `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<10-char TeamID>` | Selects the team the auto-signed profile belongs to. You can also set `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` as a build setting for each target. |

Other related build settings you'll commonly pass alongside:

| Build setting | Example | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` | `com.example.myapp` | Override the bundle ID at build time (handy in CI matrices). |
| `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY` | `"Apple Development"` / `"Apple Distribution"` | Select dev vs. distribution identity; auto-selected when `Automatic` is on. |
| `PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER` | `"My Team Profile"` | (Manual mode) Specific profile name; **omit** under automatic signing. |
| `CODE_SIGN_STYLE` | `Automatic` / `Manual` | Set per-target or at command line. |
| `DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE` / `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` / `MARKETING_VERSION` | | Override localization, build number, marketing version. |

### How automatic signing actually resolves in CI

1. Xcode looks up your Apple ID identity in the Keychain (on CI you must unlock the keychain or pre-install a "fastlane match" / App Store Connect API key).
2. With `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` + `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=...` set, `xcodebuild` asks Apple for a profile whose bundle ID matches the target's `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`.
3. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` is required on every invocation; without it, a missing profile halts the build.
4. For first-time device installs, `-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration` lets Xcode add the iPad to the team's registered device list (capped at 100/200/300 per platform per program).

> 2026 note: signing is now done under-the-hood with Apple's "secure signing" framework. From the CLI nothing changes — `xcodebuild` + `devicectl` still handle it — but Apple no longer surfaces `.mobileprovision` files in the same way; provisioning profiles are pulled from Apple's backend by the `xcodebuild` signing daemon. The four flags above are still the correct invocation.

content.4_devicectl_install_launch_terminate_on_:
### 4.1 Top-level command structure

```
devicectl [<global opts>] <subcommand> [<subcommand opts>]
```

Useful global options before any subcommand:

| Global opt | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Verbose logging to stderr. |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only warnings/errors. |
| `-t`, `--timeout <seconds>` | Override the default command timeout. |
| `-j`, `--json-output <path>` | Write machine-readable JSON to a file — ideal for CI and stable across `devicectl` versions. |
| `-l`, `--log-output <path>` | Write full logs to a file. |

### 4.2 The four commands you need

**(a) Discover devices**

```
xcrun devicectl list devices
# or for a single property you can also pipe:
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output devices.json
```

Look at the `identifier` (UDID) field of the entry whose `model`/name matches your iPad.

**(b) Install an `.app` onto the iPad**

```
xcrun devicectl device install app \
    --device <UDID> \
    /path/to/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/MyApp.app
```

Optional flags:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--terminate-running-process` | Kill the app if it's currently running before reinstalling. Useful for clean re-deployments in CI. |
| `--skip-install-verification` | Skip the post-install health check (faster, but lose the safety net). |
| `--quiet` | Silence non-error output. |

**(c) Launch the app by bundle ID**

```
xcrun devicectl device process launch \
    --device <UDID> \
    com.example.myapp
```

Optional flags:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--terminate-running-process` | Kill any running instance first. |
| `--console-pty` | Attach a pseudo-terminal and stream stdout/stderr (handy for headless runs). |
| `--stdout=<path>` / `--stderr=<path>` | Redirect launch logs to a file. |
| `--env KEY=VALUE` | Pass env vars to the launched process. |

**(d) Uninstall and terminate**

```
xcrun devicectl device process terminate --device <UDID> com.example.myapp
xcrun devicectl device uninstall app --device <UDID> com.example.myapp
```

### 4.3 Other useful subcommands

| Subcommand | What it does |
|---|---|
| `devicectl device info` | Show device UDID, model, OS version, hostname. |
| `devicectl manage devices reboot` | Reboot the connected device. |
| `devicectl device process list` | List running apps. |
| `devicectl device process spawn` | Spawn a one-off process (used internally by XCTest). |
| `devicectl device diagnostics capture` | Pull a sysdiagnose. |
| `devicectl list devices` / `list ddimages` | List connected hardware or developer disk images. |

content.5_end_to_end_ipad_deploy_pipeline_copy_p:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# ── Inputs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCHEME="MyApp"
WORKSPACE="MyApp.xcworkspace"
UDID="00008110-001A1234ABCD123D"
BUNDLE_ID="com.example.myapp"
TEAM_ID="ABCDE12345"

# ── 1. Build for the connected iPad with automatic signing ───────────────────
xcodebuild \
  -workspace  "$WORKSPACE" \
  -scheme     "$SCHEME" \
  -configuration Release \
  -destination "platform=iOS,id=$UDID" \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM_ID" \
  CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Development" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  -allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration \
  clean build

APP_PATH="build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/${SCHEME}.app"

# ── 2. Install to the physical iPad ───────────────────────────────────────────
xcrun devicectl device install app \
  --device "$UDID" \
  --terminate-running-process \
  "$APP_PATH"

# ── 3. Launch the app ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
xcrun devicectl device process launch \
  --device "$UDID" \
  --terminate-running-process \
  "$BUNDLE_ID"
```

This pipeline produces a signed `.app` for the connected iPad, installs it via `devicectl`, and launches it by bundle identifier — all from the command line, with no Xcode UI.

content.6_building_for_archive_export_testflight:
When you need an `.ipa` or `.xcarchive` rather than a directly-installable `.app`, add `archive` and `exportArchive` and pass an `ExportOptions.plist`:

```bash
xcodebuild \
  -workspace "$WORKSPACE" -scheme "$SCHEME" \
  -configuration Release \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -archivePath build/MyApp.xcarchive \
  CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM_ID" \
  CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Distribution" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  archive

xcodebuild \
  -exportArchive \
  -archivePath build/MyApp.xcarchive \
  -exportPath build/Export \
  -exportOptionsPlist ExportOptions.plist
```

Common `ExportOptions.plist` keys:

| Key | Typical value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `app-store`, `ad-hoc`, `enterprise`, `development`, `developer-id` | Determines signing/entitlements path. |
| `signingStyle` | `automatic` or `manual` | Must be `automatic` if you want `xcodebuild` to fetch profiles for you. |
| `teamID` | your 10-char team ID | Required with automatic signing. |
| `uploadSymbols` | `true` / `false` | Whether to ship dSYMs to App Store Connect. |
| `uploadBitcode` | `false` | Bitcode is deprecated; keep `false`. |
| `compileBitcode` | `false` | Same. |
| `provisioningProfiles` | `{ "com.example.myapp" = "My Profile Name"; }` | Required only with manual signing. |
| `thinning` | `none` | `thin`/`thin-for-variant` for App Store Connect. |

For App Store/TestFlight builds you usually omit `provisioningProfiles` and rely entirely on automatic signing with `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.

content.7_common_gotchas_in_2026:
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Could not find Developer Disk Image" | Xcode doesn't match the iPadOS version. | Update Xcode to the latest point release; iPadOS 18/26 features require matching Xcode. |
| "Failed to register device" in CI | `-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration` missing. | Add the flag; or pre-register the device in App Store Connect. |
| Codesign fails in headless CI | Keychain locked or signing identity missing. | `security unlock-keychain -p "$PASSWORD" ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` and import the cert (`security import ... -k ... -P ... -T /usr/bin/codesign`). |
| App fails to launch on iPad | Bundle ID mismatch / wrong provisioning profile. | Verify the bundle ID in `Info.plist` matches `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` and the profile. |
| `devicectl` hangs after a build | Old Xcode on macOS with new iPadOS, or stale `CoreDevice` cache. | Reboot, then run `sudo killall -KILL usbmuxd` and replug the device. |
| "iPhone is not available" | Device trust prompt not accepted. | Tap "Trust" on the iPad after first connect, then re-run. |
| Wants you to re-sign every build | Xcode 15+ behavior; profile missing entitlement. | Keep `-allowProvisioningUpdates` and `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set; don't forget to renew profiles. |

**Build flags (`xcodebuild`)**  
`-workspace | -project` · `-scheme` · `-configuration` · `-destination` · `-derivedDataPath` · `-archivePath` · `-archive` · `-exportArchive` · `-exportOptionsPlist` · `-allowProvisioningUpdates` · `-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration` · `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` · `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=` · `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER=` · `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=` · `OTHER_CODE_SIGN_FLAGS=`

**Deploy commands (`xcrun devicectl`)**  
`list devices` · `device install app` · `device uninstall app` · `device process launch` · `device process terminate` · `device process list` · `device info` · `device diagnostics capture` · `manage devices reboot`

**Auth helpers**  
`security unlock-keychain` · `security import` · `xcrun altool --store-password` (legacy) · `xcrun notarytool` (notary) · App Store Connect API key JSON (preferred for CI)

content.9_end_to_end_one_liner_debug_install_lau:
```bash
xcodebuild -workspace MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=00008110-001A1234ABCD123D' \
  -derivedDataPath build \
  CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates -allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration \
  build && \
xcrun devicectl device install app --device 00008110-001A1234ABCD123D --terminate-running-process \
  build/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/MyApp.app && \
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device 00008110-001A1234ABCD123D --terminate-running-process \
  com.example.myapp
```

That single shell line covers the entire "build a signed app, push it to a real iPad, and launch it" workflow using only `xcodebuild` + `devicectl`, with automatic provisioning handled entirely on the command line.
